kind: source-specific phase diagnostics, not matched-condition accuracy validation

source.document: Airbus / AEROGAL (GLG) Flight Crew Operating Manual, For A/C HC-CLF
source.pdfPageNumbering: 1-based; not the printed section page number
source.providedBy: User-supplied PDF; the original manual is not included in this repository

evidence.meaning: The sole aircraft allocated to this tailored FCOM is MSN2078 / HC-CLF / 319-112.
J0071: wing tip incorporating a tip fence.
AAT defines the fleet covered by this FCOM.
Engine equivalence list maps A319-112 to CFM56-5B6; it is not an expansion of numerical table applicability.
Embedded table footer explicitly identifies A319-112 CFM56-5B6/P.

notes: Applicable to ALL means all aircraft in the allocation table of this tailored manual, not every aircraft family named on the cover.
These tables do not directly apply to A320/CFM56-5B4, sharklet variants, NEO or Boeing.
The numerical grid is not an aircraft operating envelope or a statement that every tabulated mass is permitted for HC-CLF.

climb.reason: FCOM uses ISA+10; current mission atmosphere is ISA0. No ISA0 climb table or temperature extrapolation is provided. The model also lacks the exact CFM56-5B6/P installation standard.

descent.reason: Source explicitly ends at 1500 ft and separates approach/landing. The old fixed model allowance has no equally explicit phase boundary. Source mass convention is WEIGHT and needs a stated assumption before mission integration.

holding.reason: FCOM uses green-dot race-track at FL15 with installed-engine conditions; the current model uses max L/D and a fixed holding TSFC ratio without an altitude-dependent holding engine model. Straight-line correction only removes the documented pattern difference.

conclusions: The climb total includes takeoff; adding the existing 90 kg on top would double-count fuel.
Holding flow is per engine; descent fuel is aircraft total. Engine count must not be applied to both indiscriminately.
Descent to 1500 ft and IFR approach/landing are different phases.
The source tables do not replace A320, NEO or Boeing phases or justify a new universal TSFC correction.
Exact source-node reproduction checks data handling, not independent accuracy of a mission model using those same tables.
